transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-08-22
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jamie Ortega (Redwood AE), Sanya Patel (Redwood SE), Ellen Ramirez (Verdant Head of IT), Omar Chen (Verdant Security Lead), Priya Kapoor (Verdant Legal Counsel)
Recording note: audio quality OK, a few dropouts in the last 5 minutes

Summary:
Quick security/compliance run-through focused on data residency and KMS onboarding for an EU-only pilot.  Discussed sub-processor list, SCCs, BYOK/HSM options, audit log retention and RBAC/SSO controls. Agreed next steps around docs and a pilot.

Topics:
- EU-only deployment topology and cross-border flow limits
- KMS / BYOK / HSM integration options and key residency
- Sub-processors and contractual controls (SCCs / DPA language)
- Audit logs, retention, and export formats
- RBAC, SSO (SAML) and delegated admin model

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jamie (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll keep this focused, want to make sure we cover the residency questions and the KMS flow.  Quick intros?
[00:14] Ellen (Verdant): Hi all, Ellen here.  We're trying to lock down an EU-only path for PHI-ish telemetry, long story short legal wants to avoid any US processing.
[00:22] Omar (Verdant): Omar, security.  I'll own the technical questions about logs and key management.
[00:27] Priya (Verdant): Priya from legal, mostly contract and DPA stuff.
[00:32] Sanya (Redwood SE): Sanya with Redwood, I'll go deep on the KMS and infra side.
[00:36] Jamie: Great.  So objective: verify we can bind the data flows to an EU-tenant and make sure keys and audit trails don't cross borders.  Sanya, quick run-through of how Redwood handles region selection and routing?
[00:50] Sanya: Sure.  At a high-level, we have a routing policy that pins requests by customer or route to specific regions. For hosted customers we can provision an EU-only cluster with no egress to the US if you elect that topology.  There's also a dedicated option for more control.
[01:10] Omar: When you say "no egress" — is that a technical guarantee or a contractual one?  I'm thinking about control-plane calls, metrics, phone-home telemetry, subprocessor callbacks, etc.
[01:20] Sanya: Good point.  Practically speaking the data plane (model inference, logs, KV cache) can be kept entirely in-region.  Control-plane telemetry like aggregated metrics and some platform alerts may route to our control plane which is multi-region; we can discuss a private control-plane option where that traffic stays in customer VPC or a private deployment.
[01:39] Jamie: And from a contractual side we can add an annex that restricts cross-border processing unless Verdant provides explicit consent.  Priya, is that what you're looking for?
[01:50] Priya: Yes, along with SCCs and a clear sub-processor list.  We need to know which subprocessors would see EU data even transiently.
[01:58] Sanya: We'll share our subprocessors list. Note there are infra providers and specialized inference partners — we can mark who has access to storage or logs.  Also we have an EU-only subprocessor stack option for customers who require it.
[02:14] Ellen: Can you clarify the KMS options?  We currently use an in-house HSM for keys, and we prefer BYOK where we hold keys in our HSM.
[02:23] Sanya: Yes, we support BYOK.  Two common patterns: 1) Redwood-managed keys provisioned in an EU KMS, and 2) Customer-managed keys where Verdant uploads a wrapped key or we integrate with your KMS via a cross-account IAM role and HSM.  For the highest assurance we support an HSM-backed key with key material never leaving your HSM — we have an HSM connector that performs envelope encryption and only persistent ciphertext is stored.
[02:49] Omar: What's the key rotation process look like?  If Verdant rotates keys monthly, will that disrupt model cache or inference?
[02:57] Sanya: We have a key-rotation handshake: wrapped keys and a KMS plugin that allows live rotation. The runtime keeps a KV cache with key IDs; when a rotation happens we swap the key reference and continue serving; there can be a short TTL for cached items but no full re-ingest required. We'll share the rotation playbook.
[03:18] Priya: From a legal perspective we need to see the KMS integration guide and the exact language that says Redwood will not export key material to any non-EU subprocessors.
[03:28] Jamie: We'll include explicit language in the DPA + KMS addendum.  Sanya, note to include the HSM spec and assurance language.
[03:36] Sanya: Noted.  Also relevant: we can provide per-tenant audit logs including KMS events and key operation logs; these can be shipped to your SIEM via syslog/HTTPS endpoints, and we can keep those in EU-only storage.
[03:52] Ellen: On logs, what fields are captured?  We need IP, request id, timestamp, model id, route, and a correlation id across services.
[04:01] Sanya: We capture timestamp, request id, route, model version, response size, latency buckets, and an opaque caller id.  IP capture is configurable; default is redacted but you can elect to capture full IPs for forensic needs.  Correlation id can be passed through your request headers and we persist it.
[04:21] Omar: Retention windows?  Our policy is 90 days for most telemetry and 7 years for specific audit trails.
[04:28] Sanya: Out-of-the-box we keep live logs for 90 days; we offer extended retention for audit trails up to configurable years depending on the plan — that's an add-on.  There's also an export pipeline to cold storage if you want long-term retention in your EU bucket.
[04:45] Priya: Are audit logs tamper-evident?  For regulated audits we want append-only logs with integrity checks.
[04:52] Sanya: We support checksums and signed log exports. For highest assurance we can stream logs into your managed object store with immutability policies or to a WORM-compliant archive. We'll include examples.
[05:05] Jamie: Switching back to subprocessors — can you talk through an example where an infra provider might receive data and how you mitigate that?
[05:13] Sanya: If we use a managed database in EU region, the provider operates the disks. We limit what they see through encryption at rest + field-level encryption for sensitive fields. Also our contractual relationship with infra providers includes standard security controls and on-request audits. For customers with stricter needs we offer dedicated or private deployment where we can avoid shared infra.
[05:33] Ellen: So the private deployment option would be fully on-prem or VPC-hosted so we control networking?
[05:40] Sanya: Correct. Private deployments can be in your VPC or on-prem; control plane can be customer-managed. That eliminates most subprocessor exposure.
[05:50] Omar: About SCCs — we've been told to avoid relying solely on SCCs when there's risk of government access in third countries. What is Redwood's stance?
[05:58] Jamie: We typically combine SCCs with technical controls: EU-only processing, contractual commitments, and the ability to run a private control plane. If government access is a concern, the private or dedicated routes are advisable.
[06:10] Priya: Can we get an redlined example clause that says "no onward transfer without written consent"?
[06:16] Jamie: Yes, we'll draft that — subject to negotiation, we can add strict restrictions on onward transfers and require notice.
[06:22] Ellen: On the operational side, if we pick EU-only hosted, what's the SLA and latency expectation? Our app is Europe-facing, low-latency requirement.
[06:31] Sanya: Our EU clusters are optimized for EU latency; typical p95 generation times match our public benchmarks. SLA-wise for hosted EU we can commit to a latency SLO and uptime. For stricter latency guarantees you'd pick Dedicated capacity in-region.
[06:46] Omar: One more technical: what about model telemetry or embeddings that might be stored for quality monitoring? Those could leak PII.
[06:54] Sanya: We have an opt-in for data collection for eval/quality. By default embeddings/outputs are not persisted beyond session TTL unless you opt into monitoring. For EU-only tenancy we can restrict storage to EU and provide ability to anonymize or hash tokens before storage.
[07:10] Priya: We'll need to ensure that any monitoring is subject to our explicit consent and that retention is governed by our DPA annex.
[07:17] Jamie: Agreed.  We'll make that a checkbox in the contract and the console has toggles for enabling monitoring per tenant.
[07:24] [08:00] Unidentified (background): yeah..
[07:26] Ellen: About SSO — we use SAML with a few groups mapped to roles. Can we do RBAC that maps to your console roles?
[07:34] Sanya: Yes, we map SAML groups to Redwood roles. We support SCIM for user provisioning and fine-grained RBAC, including tenant-level admins and read-only analysts.
[07:45] Omar: Do you support delegated admin where our security team can see logs but not change keys?
[07:50] Sanya: Yes — RBAC rules can prevent key operations while allowing log viewing. You can also restrict key rotation to specific roles.
[07:58] Priya: Any certifications we should be aware of? SOC 2 Type II is available; ISO 27001 in progress for the EU region?
[08:05] Jamie: We have SOC 2 Type II and we're pursuing ISO 27001; for EU customers we can provide the SOC report and an ISO timeline.
[08:14] Ellen: On subprocessors again, will you provide notification windows for adding new subprocessors? We require 30 days notice and ability to object.
[08:21] Jamie: We typically provide a 30-day notice for material subprocessor changes and an objection mechanism for a small set of regulated customers. We'll include this in the DPA.
[08:30] Omar: For the EU-only pilot we want to perform an on-site inspection or a security workshop — is that feasible?
[08:37] Sanya: We do security workshops and can schedule a remote technical deep-dive. On-site inspections are possible for private/dedicated customers — for hosted we can offer a virtual walk-through and evidence package.
[08:51] Priya: Can you confirm there are no US-based backups of EU data by default?
[08:56] Sanya: By default EU clusters replicate within EU region only. Backups can be configured to stay in EU. We avoid cross-border backups unless customer opts in.
[09:07] Ellen: What about incident response — who notifies whom and timelines?
[09:12] Jamie: We commit to notify Verdant within 72 hours for incidents affecting personal data, and provide regular updates. For high-severity incidents we do 24-hour initial notification. We'll include our IR playbook.
[09:25] Omar: For the audit logs export — can we get them in a parquet format to ingest into our data lake?
[09:30] Sanya: Yes, we support JSON and parquet exports via our export API. We can push to your EU S3 bucket or deliver via secure transfer.
[09:38] Ellen: You mentioned a UI toggle for region pinning earlier. Can we demo that quickly?
[09:44] Sanya: I can share a screenshot and a short flow, but for this call I'll describe: under Tenant > Region, you select "EU-only" and the system will provision resources in the EU pool, and the new routing policy applies. For production we'll confirm the provisioning time — usually a few hours to a day for hosted.
[10:06] Jamie: Let's talk about proof — Priya wants contractual language, Omar wants technical proof. Is a pilot cluster with audit logs delivered to Verdant's EU bucket acceptable?
[10:18] Omar: Yes, that's what we'd like — we want to run synthetic traffic and verify there are no egress events.
[10:24] Priya: And we'd like the DPA updated before any pilot with real data.
[10:29] Jamie: Totally reasonable. We'll make the pilot use synthetic data unless you sign the DPA addendum.
[10:34] [12:00] Speaker 6: gah audio..
[10:36] Ellen: For KMS, are there any constraints on algorithm or length? We run RSA-4096 for signing and AES-256 for encryption.
[10:44] Sanya: We support RSA and modern symmetric ciphers; the envelope supports AES-256-GCM commonly. For signing we support RSA and ECDSA depending on your needs. We'll add the cipher suite table to the KMS guide.
[10:57] Omar: Are there any telemetry packets that still go to US for feature flags or model telemetry?
[11:03] Sanya: Feature flags can be region-localized. Some aggregated product telemetry is routed to a global observability plane, but we have a customer option to restrict product telemetry to EU or to self-host observability.
[11:17] Priya: Regarding subprocessors in non-EU jurisdictions — if a subprocessor triggers lawful access, how do you communicate to Verdant?
[11:25] Jamie: We push notice as soon as we can, and we have an escalation process. For customers with heightened requirements we recommend private/dedicated deployment to reduce that surface.
[11:36] Ellen: Can you provide a timeline for the DPA + SCC annex? We need it early next week if possible.
[11:42] Jamie: We'll aim to send a first draft by Monday (2025-08-25).
[11:46] Sanya: I'll attach a KMS playbook and the HSM connector spec in the same email.
[11:52] Ellen: For the POC cluster, what telemetry will you show: full audit, KMS events, network flows?
[11:58] Sanya: We'll surface request-level audit logs, KMS operation logs (encrypt/decrypt key IDs), and control-plane provisioning logs. Network flow logs can be included as VPC flow logs if in your VPC.
[12:11] Omar: How do you handle data subject requests (DSRs)? If a user requests deletion, how does it propagate to model caches?
[12:21] Sanya: We have a purge pipeline that deletes tenant-specific persisted artifacts and marks cached KV entries for eviction; immediate in-memory cache evictions are supported for sensitive records. We will document the SLA for DSR propagation.
[12:36] Priya: Make sure deletion is logged and an audit record is provided.
[12:40] Sanya: That's standard, we log delete operations and who triggered them.
[12:44] Jamie: Quick recap/agreements so far: 1) Redwood to provide DPA + SCC annex and subprocessor list, 2) KMS integration docs + HSM spec, 3) pilot EU-only cluster with synthetic traffic, 4) audit log export in parquet to Verdant EU storage for verification. Anything missing?
[13:03] Omar: Also the key rotation playbook and retention config options.
[13:07] Ellen: And the notice period for subprocessor changes + objection process.
[13:10] Priya: IR playbook and SOC 2 report.
[13:14] Jamie: We'll include all that.  Any blocking legal terms we should flag now Priya?
[13:20] Priya: The main one is the onward transfer clause and the retention of backups.  We may ask for a contractual guarantee about backup location and access controls.
[13:31] Jamie: We'll propose specific backup language in the addendum.
[13:34] [15:00] Background noise - small kids playing
[13:37] Ellen: One last thing - do you have a mechanism for data residency attestations? A signed letter or statement for auditors?
[13:45] Sanya: Yes, we can provide a signed attestation and environment diagrams showing region boundaries and control plane options.
[13:52] Omar: If we do the pilot and it's successful, what's the rollout path to production? How long to expand capacity?
[13:59] Sanya: For hosted EU-to-prod it's a matter of provisioning additional capacity in the EU cluster and adjusting routing policies; typical timeline is a few days to a couple weeks depending on committed capacity. For Dedicated it's longer because of reserved capacity procurement.
[14:15] Priya: Regarding indemnity and liability caps — we'll review the contract but wanted to note potential redlines from procurement.
[14:22] Jamie: Understood, procurement tends to want tailored limits for regulated data. We'll loop in contracts post-pilot.
[14:29] Ellen: Any dependencies on our side to enable SCIM/SAML or KMS access?
[14:34] Sanya: For SAML/SCIM we'll need metadata and group mappings. For KMS-BYOK we need an integration account and API/service principal with appropriate permissions and an endpoint for HSM connector. We'll send a checklist.
[14:49] Omar: Do you do background checks on staff that might access logs in the EU region?
[14:54] Jamie: We have internal policies and background checks for ops staff with admin access; we can provide a summary of the personnel security program.
[14:59] Priya: Last question: are customers allowed to request a copy of the SOC report under NDA?
[15:05] Jamie: Yes, SOC reports are shared under NDA. We'll send that with the other docs.
[15:10] Ellen: Great. When should we reconvene?
[15:14] Jamie: Suggest we reconvene after Verdant reviews the DPA and after Sanya ships the KMS playbook — does the week of Sept 8 work to start pilot verification?
[15:22] Omar: That works for us.
[15:24] Priya: Works for legal too.
[15:26] Jamie: OK, I'll send notes and the deliverables timeline. Thanks, everyone.
[15:31] Ellen: Thanks.
[15:34] Meeting end 15:18 UTC (call length ~48m; a couple of audio blips near 36m and final 5m)
